title: Visual Detection of Multiple Nucleic Acids in a Capillary Array
protocol: Clean the stainless-steel mold by detergent.
Wash the stainless-steel mold with ethanol.
Rinse the stainless-steel mold with deionized water.
Dry the mold using nitrogen.
Put on safety goggles, lab uniform, and chemical protective gloves.
Place capillaries into a beaker.
Clean capillaries with 30 mL acetone for 15 minutes to remove organic matter.
Wash capillaries with deionized water.
Pour 10 mL of H2O2 into the beaker containing capillaries.
Slowly add 30 mL of H2SO4 to the H2O2 in the beaker, shaking gently to prevent overheating.
Ensure the piranha solution completely covers the capillaries for at least 30 minutes.
Clean capillaries thoroughly by shaking an acid cylinder during the process.
Wash away piranha solution with a large amount of water.
Wash capillaries with ethanol and deionized water, each for 5 minutes.
Dry the capillaries in a drying oven.
Weight out PDMS base and curing reagents in a ratio of 1:1 in a 50 mL tube.
Mix thoroughly for about 5 minutes with a glass rod.
Place the mixture in a vacuum bell jar for 30 minutes to de-gas.
Pour the degassed mixture slowly into the cylinder of a stainless-steel mold.
Allow the PDMS to stand for 5 minutes to remove bubbles naturally.
Pour the mixture into the cylinder and let it cure for 3 hours at 60 °C in a drying oven.
Remove the mold by pulling it out after curing is complete.
Cut the margin of the mold with a scalpel to separate PDMS from the cylinder.
Wash PDMS three times with ethanol and deionized water.
Dry the PDMS support with nitrogen gas.
Soak the lower surface of the PDMS support in a super-hydrophobic coat for 1 second.
Dry the treated PDMS at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Insert the cleaned 4 mm capillaries into the holes of the PDMS support.
Leave 0.5 mm of the capillaries outside the top surface of the PDMS support.
Ensure the ends of capillaries are on the same level.
Add 15 µL super-hydrophobic coat onto the top surface of the PDMS support.
Air dry the super-hydrophobic modified capillary array.
Prepare primer solution by weighting out 0.65 g chitosan and dissolving it into 50 mL deionized water, adjusting pH to 4.5-5.5 with acetic acid.
Add 1.6 µL of the mixture of one set of primers to fill one corresponding capillary according to a pre-designed order.
Anchor the array in a transparent well of a standard flat bottom 96-well plate and dry at 60 °C for at least 2 h.
Assemble the cassette as follows.
Put a loading adaptor onto the top of anchored array.
Make sure the dish of the adaptor just covers the exposed parts of all ten capillaries.
Prepare the LAMP reaction mix as per the specified protocol.
Add reagents to the mixture according to the chosen order.
Vortex the reaction mixture for 5 seconds after adding calcein.
Gently invert the tube 20 times after Bst polymerase is added.
Mix 11.6 μL ddH2O with LAMP components.
Add 2.0 μL MgSO4 (100 mM) to the mixture.
Include 1.4 μL dNTPs (25 mM).
Add 4.0 μL Betaine (5 M).
Mix in 2.5 μL Buffer (10x).
Add 0.5 μL Calcein (1.25 mM).
Include 0.5 μL MnCl2 (25 mM).
Pipette 1.5 μL Bst polymerase (8 U/μL) into the mixture.
Mix in 1.0 μL plant DNA (10 ng/μL).
Ensure the total volume reaches 25.0 μL.
Load reagents and seal the cassette.
Pipette 20 µL LAMP reaction mixture using a standard 100 µL tip.
Insert the pipette tip into the inlet of the loading adaptor to lock it.
Gently inject the reaction mixture into the dish of the adaptor.
Remove the adaptor with the locked tip after injection is complete.
Seal the well by a PCR-compatible transparent sealing film.
Incubate the capillary array in an incubator at 63 °C for 1 h.
Acquire images of the fluorescence emission.
Fix a UV filter on the top surface of a small hand-held UV LED flashlight to filter the visible light.
Excite the dissociated calcein to emit fluorescence with the UV flashlight.
Capture images from the top of the capillary array by either a digital camera or a smartphone.
Ensure that the camera is zoomed in on the area of the capillaries as much as possible to get high quality, clear images.
Open the image using image analysis software.
Select "Image>Mold>Grayscale>Yes".
Select "Image>Mold>16bit>Yes".
Convert the image to 16-bit TIFF format by selecting "File>Save as>format>TIFF".
Drag the 16-bit TIFF format image into the interface of the microarray analysis software.
Select the wavelength of "532 nm" and a color of "green" to display the image.
Create a new block to locate the fluorescence signal from the capillaries.
Select "Tools>New blocks" and input the number of columns and rows as "1;1".
Input the number of columns and rows as "2;5" in the 'features' interface.
Right click and select "Features" model.
Adjust the location and diameter to fit the fluorescence area of capillaries.
Select "Analyze" to extract the value of fluorescence intensity.
Select "File>save settings as" to save the blocks documents.
Select "File>save results as" to save the fluorescence intensity results.
